claim: Tim17 forms a lipid-exposed cavity that is the protein-conducting path
key_finding: Yeast TIM23 complex structure resolves a Tim17 cavity open to the bilayer with a negatively charged entrance; Tim23 cavity faces the opposite direction and is structural
confidence_limits: High. Yeast; human TIMM17A/TIMM23 inferred by homology

claim: Same cavity assignment in an independent TIM23 structure
key_finding: Independent structure confirms Tim17 as the translocation path subunit

claim: The Tim17 cavity binds an alpha-helical topogenic-sequence mimic
key_finding: Stendomycin occupies the Tim17 lateral cavity, giving an empirical definition of the conducting site used here as the probe
confidence_limits: High for the site definition; the probe is an inhibitor, not a substrate

key_finding: TM-score of the TIMMDC1 AlphaFold TM core (80-230) to Tim17 = 0.745 and to Tim23 = 0.765, versus 0.251 to OXA1L
context: AlphaFold Q9NPL8 v6, TM-align-style superposition written for this run
confidence_limits: Medium-high. Predicted coordinates; pLDDT 82.8 over the TM core

claim: TIMMDC1 lacks the acidic cavity lining
key_finding: Acidic residues lining the free volume at the stendomycin site: Tim17 5, Tim22 human 5, Tim22 yeast 5, TIMMDC1 1, Tim23 0
context: Six structures superposed into one frame
confidence_limits: Medium-high. Side-chain positions in a predicted model are less certain than residue identity

claim: The absence is conserved, not an artifact of one model
key_finding: 0 of 22 cavity-equivalent positions are acidic in a majority of 250-315 metazoan TIMMDC1 orthologs, while the TIMM17A set D15/D16/D77/E127 is 96.0-99.6% acidic across 250 TIMM17A orthologs
context: UniProt/OrthoDB-derived ortholog sets, pairwise global alignment to the human reference
confidence_limits: Medium. Fisher test on acidic-majority positions p=0.061, so the argument rests on the matched-position contrast

key_finding: Free volume at the stendomycin site: Tim17 3459 A^3, TIMMDC1 2654 A^3, Tim23 2822 A^3, OXA1L 932 A^3; a near-invariant GxxxGxxxGxxxG repeat (G191/G195/G199/G203, 98-99% identity in 315 orthologs) lines the TM core
confidence_limits: Medium. A groove remains; the hypothesis wording 'lacks the cavity' is too absolute

claim: TIMMDC1 is a complex I membrane-arm assembly factor
key_finding: TIMMDC1 (C3orf1) associates with complex I assembly intermediates and the MCIA complex; knockdown impairs complex I assembly
confidence_limits: High for the assembly role, silent on insertase activity

claim: Loss of TIMMDC1 causes complex I deficiency
key_finding: A deep-intronic variant creating aberrant splicing of TIMMDC1 causes mitochondrial complex I deficiency in patients
confidence_limits: High for the disease link; loss-of-function phenotype does not identify the molecular activity

claim: Current GO annotation does not claim transport
key_finding: QuickGO returns 6 distinct terms for Q9NPL8; no transporter, insertase, channel or transmembrane-transport term in any aspect
confidence_limits: Database-level. Accurate as retrieved in this run

claim: A route to insertase over-annotation exists
key_finding: TIMMDC1 carries PF02466 'Tim17/Tim22/Tim23/Pmp24 family' and UniProt states 'Belongs to the Tim17/Tim22/Tim23 family'; InterPro IPR055299 and PANTHER PTHR13002 already separate it
confidence_limits: Database-level. Risk is latent, not realised

claim: A nucleoplasm CC annotation conflicts with the mitochondrial inner membrane
key_finding: A single IDA nucleoplasm line from immunofluorescence sits against 7 Reactome TAS lines for mitochondrial inner membrane and IBA/IDA/HTP mitochondrion lines
